items.summary: A collection of my personal favourite snaps of 2014. First one I’ve…
items.content_html: A collection of my personal favourite snaps of 2014. First one I’ve put up here is one of a Heron I captured in Richmond Upon Thames, was lucky that these birds are known to stay still for long periods of time (my shutter speed isn’t the fastest of things!), others include my HDR take on the Natural History Museum, London and one of the ‘big cheese’ I set-up & took on a cold night in November.

items.title: London & Local 2013
items.summary: A collection of my personal favourite snaps of 2013, the Love sculpture by Robert Indiana probably…
items.content_html: A collection of my personal favourite snaps of 2013, the Love sculpture by Robert Indiana probably being my pick (I have a huge canvas of this in my room), and for more info on his work check out the Robert Indiana page at Artsy. I also like the boat drifting off down the River Thames with The Shard in the background, the train tracks one is from Hampton Court station ~ risky job this photography business haha..

items.summary: I’ve picked out some of my favourite snaps of 2012 here, really…
items.content_html: I’ve picked out some of my favourite snaps of 2012 here, really happy with the motorbike in Camden Town, the guy came along whilst composing the shot ~ he was quite happy to be in it (or so it seemed I hope!). The guy playing surf guitar was rockin’ the tube station, caught him between cords, St Pauls Cathedral was pulled off by use of a tripod and getting in the way of foreign tourists, was chuffed with that! and a felt obliged to put the Carnaby Street one in there for obvious reasons..

items.content_html: After watching a great series of programmes on architecture, Architecture at the Crossroads, I was inspired to hunt out some of the great postmodern/ brutalist architecture of London from the 60/70/80s that are still standing today. I will be adding photos to this series as I find these unknown gems of building history…

items.title: Photo Series - Barbican Centre, London
items.summary: My first encounter with this awesome bit of concrete jungle situated in…
items.content_html:
My first encounter with this awesome bit of concrete jungle situated in the center of London was back in the 90’s when myself and some friends went on a skateboarding mission to find the famous ‘Barbican banks’ that were at the time skateable (with the risk of getting a bucket shower from the residents above mind you), rolling around this place was like being in a futuristic skateboarding movie! the spacious ‘all brick banks’ with there lush green grass made great carving and the area was usually very quiet so you would have it all to yourself…

Forward to 2017 and recently I’ve made a few trips into the Barbican for a different reason, to take some photos (although I have had my cruzer board on me, and the temptation to have a little roll is always been there, the security and now skate-stopped banks lead me to believe its probably easier to carry the thing around here), it’s still got that awe about it though, all that crazy crete, towering over weird shapes and colourful flower beds – it’s still a peaceful place to walk around for an hour or so and admire the timeless design. I’m sure I’ll be going back to see if I missed anything plus they regularly have some good art exhibits on, and maybe, just maybe a little silent roll on the ol’ cruzer…

Note: Great site about everything Barbican over here: barbicanliving.co.uk
